standards.description: Help students estimate limits from graphs and tables and interpret one-sided limits and limits at infinity in context.
standards.ccssText: Estimate limits from graphs and numerical tables; interpret one-sided limits and their relationship to two-sided limits; evaluate limits at infinity and describe end behavior; identify when a limit does not exist.

standards.description: Teach students to apply limit laws and evaluate limits algebraically, including indeterminate 0/0 forms by factoring, rationalizing, or using conjugates.
standards.ccssText: Apply sum, difference, product, quotient, and power limit laws; resolve indeterminate 0/0 forms by factoring, canceling, or rationalizing; evaluate trigonometric limits using special limits lim(sin x/x) = 1 and lim((1-cos x)/x) = 0.

standards.description: Help students define continuity at a point and on an interval, classify types of discontinuities, and apply the Intermediate Value Theorem.
standards.ccssText: Define continuity at a point using the three-part definition (limit exists, function defined, limit equals function value); identify removable, jump, and infinite discontinuities; apply the Intermediate Value Theorem to verify existence of roots or values.

standards.description: Guide students to evaluate limits as x approaches positive or negative infinity and use results to identify horizontal and vertical asymptotes.
standards.ccssText: Evaluate limits as x approaches positive or negative infinity by analyzing dominant terms; use limits to identify horizontal asymptotes; evaluate limits resulting in infinity to identify vertical asymptotes.

standards.description: Introduce the derivative as the limit of a difference quotient, helping students interpret it as instantaneous rate of change and slope of the tangent line.
standards.ccssText: Define the derivative f'(x) = lim[h->0] (f(x+h)-f(x))/h; interpret the derivative as instantaneous rate of change and as the slope of the tangent line; identify when a function is not differentiable (corners, cusps, vertical tangents, discontinuities).

standards.description: Teach students to apply the power, constant, sum, difference, product, and quotient rules to differentiate polynomial and rational functions.
standards.ccssText: Apply the constant rule, power rule, constant multiple rule, sum and difference rules, product rule, and quotient rule to differentiate polynomial, rational, and algebraic functions; find equations of tangent and normal lines.

standards.description: Help students apply the chain rule to differentiate composite functions, including repeated applications for nested compositions.
standards.ccssText: Apply the chain rule dy/dx = (dy/du)(du/dx) to differentiate composite functions; identify inner and outer functions; apply the chain rule in combination with product and quotient rules.

standards.skillName: Derivatives of Trig, Exponential, and Log Functions
standards.description: Teach students to differentiate the six trigonometric functions, natural exponential function, and natural and general logarithmic functions.
standards.ccssText: Differentiate sin x, cos x, tan x, csc x, sec x, cot x, e^x, a^x, ln x, and log_a x; apply these rules in combination with product, quotient, and chain rules.

standards.description: Guide students to use implicit differentiation to find dy/dx for curves defined implicitly, including finding slopes of tangent lines.
standards.ccssText: Differentiate both sides of an equation with respect to x using the chain rule for y-terms; solve for dy/dx; apply to find slopes of tangent lines to implicitly defined curves such as circles, ellipses, and foliums.

standards.description: Help students set up and solve related rates problems by identifying related variables and differentiating their relationship with respect to time.
standards.ccssText: Identify quantities that change with respect to time; write an equation relating those quantities; differentiate implicitly with respect to t; substitute known values to find the desired rate of change.

standards.description: Teach students to use the tangent line to approximate function values near a known point and understand the concept of differentials.
standards.ccssText: Use the tangent line L(x) = f(a) + f'(a)(x - a) to approximate f(x) near x = a; define differentials dy = f'(x) dx; apply linear approximation to estimate values in real-world contexts.

standards.description: Help students state and apply the Mean Value Theorem and understand Rolle's Theorem as a special case with equal endpoints.
standards.ccssText: State the Mean Value Theorem: if f is continuous on [a,b] and differentiable on (a,b), then there exists c in (a,b) such that f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a); apply MVT to prove inequalities and analyze function behavior; state Rolle's Theorem as a special case.

standards.skillName: Increasing, Decreasing, and the First Derivative Test
standards.description: Guide students to use the sign of the first derivative to determine intervals of increase and decrease and classify local extrema.
standards.ccssText: Use the first derivative to find critical numbers and determine intervals where f is increasing or decreasing; apply the First Derivative Test to classify local maxima and minima; identify when no local extreme exists at a critical number.

standards.skillName: Concavity and the Second Derivative Test
standards.description: Teach students to use the second derivative to determine concavity and locate inflection points, and classify extrema using the Second Derivative Test.
standards.ccssText: Use the sign of f'' to determine intervals of concavity and identify inflection points where concavity changes; apply the Second Derivative Test to classify local extrema at critical numbers where f'(c) = 0.

standards.description: Help students solve real-world optimization problems by setting up an objective function, finding critical points, and verifying the nature of the extreme.
standards.ccssText: Identify the quantity to optimize and the constraint; write the objective function in one variable; find critical numbers and use the first or second derivative test to verify a maximum or minimum; interpret results in context.

standards.description: Teach students to apply L'Hopital's Rule to evaluate limits in the indeterminate forms 0/0 and infinity/infinity.
standards.ccssText: Apply L'Hopital's Rule to evaluate limits of indeterminate forms 0/0 and infinity/infinity; verify the indeterminate form before applying; apply the rule repeatedly when necessary; convert other indeterminate forms (0 times infinity, 1^infinity, etc.) to 0/0 or infinity/infinity.

standards.description: Help students approximate area under a curve using left, right, and midpoint Riemann sums and understand the definite integral as the limit of these sums.
standards.ccssText: Approximate the area under a curve using left, right, midpoint, and trapezoidal sums; define the definite integral as the limit of Riemann sums; interpret the definite integral as signed area; understand properties of definite integrals.

standards.description: Teach both parts of the Fundamental Theorem: using antiderivatives to evaluate definite integrals and differentiating integral-defined functions.
standards.ccssText: State and apply Part 1 of the FTC: d/dx[integral from a to x of f(t) dt] = f(x); state and apply Part 2: the definite integral of f from a to b equals F(b) - F(a) where F is any antiderivative of f; understand the connection between differentiation and integration.

standards.description: Help students find antiderivatives of power, exponential, logarithmic, and trigonometric functions and express results with the constant of integration.
standards.ccssText: Find antiderivatives of x^n (n not -1), 1/x, e^x, a^x, sin x, cos x, sec^2 x, and other basic functions; write indefinite integrals with the constant of integration C; verify antiderivatives by differentiation.

standards.description: Teach students to apply substitution to evaluate integrals of composite functions and properly change limits of integration for definite integrals.
standards.ccssText: Identify an appropriate substitution u = g(x) and rewrite the integral in terms of u; compute du; evaluate the integral and back-substitute; when evaluating definite integrals, change limits to u-values or back-substitute before evaluating.

standards.description: Guide students to set up and evaluate integrals to find the area of regions bounded by two or more curves, integrating with respect to x or y.
standards.ccssText: Find the area between two curves by integrating the difference of the top and bottom functions with respect to x, or right and left functions with respect to y; identify intersection points to determine limits of integration.

standards.description: Help students find volumes of solids formed by revolving a region about an axis using the disk, washer, and shell methods.
standards.ccssText: Use the disk method V = pi * integral(R^2 dx), washer method V = pi * integral((R^2 - r^2) dx), and cylindrical shell method V = 2pi * integral(r * h dx) to find volumes of solids of revolution about horizontal and vertical axes.

standards.description: Help students interpret definite integrals as net change in a quantity and apply this concept to displacement, distance traveled, and other accumulation contexts.
standards.ccssText: Interpret the definite integral of a rate of change as the total (net) change in the quantity; distinguish between net displacement (integral of velocity) and total distance traveled (integral of speed); apply to other contexts such as population growth or flow rate.

standards.description: Teach students to compute the average value of a function over an interval and apply the Mean Value Theorem for Integrals to identify a point where the function equals its average.
standards.ccssText: Compute the average value of f on [a,b] using f_avg = (1/(b-a)) * integral from a to b of f(x) dx; apply the Mean Value Theorem for Integrals to guarantee a value c where f(c) equals the average value.
